reference README.md:51 — 'On a fresh install, the installer scripts start onboarding automatically'

candidates.name: mini-ork onboard: credential detection + verified-probe wizard
evidence: git -C $REF show HEAD:docs/start/wizard.md:115-126 — 'Detect configured models, API-key environment variables, supported local AI CLIs, and already installed tool-capable models from reachable Ollama or LM Studio servers … Only that connection is tested with a real completion'
git -C $REF show HEAD:docs/start/onboarding-overview.md:11-12,36 — 'Every path establishes inference first … verifies a real completion'
mini-ork README.md:275-277 — 'For a real run, review .mini-ork/config/agents.yaml, authenticate the CLI or configure the providers it names' (manual reading before first value)
mini-ork mini_ork/cli/validate.py:30-35 — a lane liveness probe already exists ('one cached 1-token probe per configured lane, ten-minute TTL')
mini-ork mini_ork/cli/main.py:2141-2189 — doctor's provider preflight is presence-only ('GLM_API_KEY unset; run: mini-ork providers configure glm')
candidates.why: The cliff between dry run and first real run is the credential wall. OpenClaw's detection reuses what the visitor already has (a Claude/Codex CLI login on PATH, an env key, a local model server) and verifies it with a real completion before saying 'Inference ready' — converting 'go get an API key' into 'press 1 to reuse the claude CLI you already have.'
candidates.first_step: Add mini_ork/cli/onboard.py: detect claude/codex CLIs via shutil.which, env keys and vault entries via provider_environment(), and reachable OpenAI-compatible locals via the openai-chat kind; probe each candidate using validate.py's lane probe; write the winner via mini-ork providers configure / agents.yaml; register in _build_default_registry().

candidates.name: mini-ork triage: sanitized diagnosis bundle handed to a coding agent
evidence: reference docs/cli/triage.md:9-40 — detection order (codex, claude, pi, opencode, …); 'The prompt includes the OpenClaw version, platform … prioritized Doctor findings with repair hints'; archive 'excludes secrets, tokens, raw chat payloads, and raw logs'
git -C $REF show HEAD:docs/start/getting-started.md:158-172 — 'One command turns the current state of your install into a diagnosis you can act on' (openclaw triage)
mini-ork docs/operator/provider-triage.md — triage doc exists but is drift-panel-specific (Layer 2b README drift), not a first-run path
mini-ork mini_ork/cli/lane_preflight.py:532-556 — blocked runs emit good fix: lines, but nothing bundles run state for an agent or a human
candidates.why: mini-ork IS an agent dispatcher; 'mini-ork diagnosed its own broken setup by dispatching a repair prompt to my own claude CLI' is a shareable, on-brand moment. It also rescues the newcomer whose first real run died on a stale engine pointer or missing key — exactly the user who unstars and leaves.
candidates.first_step: New mini_ork/cli/triage_cmd.py: collect version + engine commit (_engine_commit in main.py), doctor output, last run's lane_preflight/verdict.json/stderr tail from .mini-ork/runs/<id>/, emit a redacted bounded prompt (allowlist discipline of mini_ork/dispatch/secrets.py), then print the handoff command or dispatch one bounded repair turn through mini-ork's own lanes.

candidates.name: mini-ork doctor --fix: from presence report to guided repair
evidence: reference docs/cli/doctor.md:9-19 — 'Health checks and quick fixes … --fix'; seven doc pages including 'Gateway and service recovery'
mini-ork mini_ork/cli/main.py:2141-2189 — _doctor_handler prints [OK]/[MISSING]/[WARN] and names fixes inline ('run: mini-ork providers configure glm', 'run mini-ork migrate') but executes none
candidates.why: Doctor is the command every stuck visitor runs first; one that ends with 'run mini-ork doctor --fix to repair these 3 findings' converts a dead end into progress. mini-ork's doctor already knows every fix — it makes the human retype them.
candidates.first_step: Extend _doctor_handler with --fix: for each WARN it already emits, run the remediation it already names (interactive providers configure <family> for unset keys; mini-ork migrate when _db_engine_version lags; mini-ork install --force for a stale managed command), printing one line per repair.

candidates.name: First-60-seconds ladder + first-run FAQ

candidates.name: Interrupted-run resume as the default story
evidence: git -C $REF show HEAD:docs/start/wizard.md:26-27 — 'Interrupted baseline setup resumes on the next run'

candidates.name: Verified install tail: version stamp + post-install self-check

candidates.name: Browser success view (mini-ork dashboard-equivalent)
evidence: reference README.md:62-66 — 'openclaw dashboard … opens the Control UI in your browser. If it loads, everything is working'

gap_analysis.miniork_today: examples/00-demo.sh is a complete offline dry-run demo (temp project, init, doctor, synthetic kickoff, run, artifact inspection); README:256-268 documents a six-step manual first workflow instead; the demo script is never mentioned in Start-here.
gap_analysis.gap: No 'mini-ork demo' subcommand in _build_default_registry() (mini_ork/cli/main.py:2180-2200); the demo requires knowing the checkout path and running bash; the example README's copy line uses a personal absolute path (~\/ps\/mini-ork) that fails elsewhere.

gap_analysis.miniork_today: doctor's provider preflight (main.py:2141-2189) is presence-only with configure hints; providers status/configure exists (providers.py:29-32); validate.py Check 5 probes configured lanes with a cached 1-token probe; secrets fail closed (dispatch/secrets.py).
gap_analysis.gap: No detection of credentials the visitor already has (CLIs on PATH, env keys, vault, local servers), no guided sequence, and no real-completion verification step that declares 'inference ready' — the README's real-run step is 'review agents.yaml, authenticate the CLI or configure the providers it names'.

gap_analysis.miniork_today: doctor reports issues read-only; lane_preflight emits per-lane reasons and a fix: line (lane_preflight.py:532-556); run artifacts (verdict.json, execute_stderr, lane_preflight JSON) persist under .mini-ork/runs/<id>/; docs/operator/provider-triage.md covers drift-panel providers only.
gap_analysis.gap: No triage command that bundles sanitized state (version, engine commit, doctor findings, last-run stderr) into an agent-ready prompt and hands it to a detected coding agent or a mini-ork lane.

gap_analysis.miniork_today: _doctor_handler (main.py:2141-2189) prints [OK]/[MISSING]/[WARN] across tools, engine-vs-DB drift, provider env vars, and vault backends, and names remediations inline.
gap_analysis.gap: No --fix posture: the named remediations (providers configure <family>, mini-ork migrate, install --force) are not executable from doctor; no repair success/failure reporting.

gap_analysis.miniork_today: validate.py ships a Fix:-hint convention for pre-run findings; docs/operator/ covers operators (env-vars, provider-triage, scheduler-retry), not newcomers.
gap_analysis.gap: No symptom-first first-run ladder with expected-good output, no first-run FAQ; error messages (lane_preflight fix: lines) do not link to any self-serve recovery doc.

gap_analysis.miniork_today: run --resume / resume / recover / rollback exist; run_resume.py:131-181 resolves home/state.db, hard-errors on unknown run ids, re-dispatches only the plan's redispatch set.
gap_analysis.gap: Interruption is invisible in the first-run path: no banner naming the interrupted run id and the exact --resume command, and README's first-workflow section never mentions resume for real runs.

gap_analysis.miniork_today: install.sh execs full_install.py which ends with a success line plus one providers hint (full_install.py:148-149); _version_handler prints a static version string (main.py:2194-2197).
gap_analysis.gap: No post-install verification or first-success pointer; version output disagrees across surfaces (0.9.0 vs help 'v0.1' vs example doc '0.1.0'); no engine/venv facts in the version line.

gap_analysis.miniork_today: The openai-chat provider kind (dispatch/openai_chat_transport.py) already supports local OpenAI-compatible endpoints like vLLM; dry run (MINI_ORK_DRY_RUN=1) is the only key-free path.
gap_analysis.gap: Dry run records no task_runs row (examples/00-demo.sh:73), so no real verified run completes without a credential; no local-lane default or localhost:11434 fallback offered anywhere in onboarding or README.

gap_analysis.miniork_today: README:235-241 documents the Windows path as five manual winget installs plus py -3 scripts/full_install.py.
gap_analysis.gap: No install.ps1 one-liner; the Windows newcomer performs by hand what the Unix newcomer gets in one curl.

gap_analysis.miniork_today: serve.py exposes a local observability API; board serves the IDE; the UI is a Rust/Zed fork in the ui/ submodule that cannot be built from this repo (docs/UI.md), and the web frontend was deliberately removed.
gap_analysis.gap: No human-visible success view a newcomer can open in one command — but filling it contradicts the project's own architecture decision, so the gap is arguably intentional.

open_questions: Would the maintainers accept an interactive wizard in the CLI (A2), given mini-ork's operator-first, no-daemon minimalism — or should onboarding be a non-interactive 'mini-ork onboard --check' that prints a plan? A negative answer demotes A2 and promotes A4/A5.
Is a PyPI publish planned? 'pipx run mini-ork demo' would be the true npx equivalent and would change A1's shape (no clone at all before first value).
Will the dry-run no-task_runs-row behavior change (examples/00-demo.sh:73)? If dry runs record state, A1's verified-success story strengthens and A8's urgency drops.
What share of the target audience is on native Windows vs WSL — this drives A9's rank — and is there CI capacity to keep a PowerShell installer honest?
For A8, can mini-ork's verifier gates pass on typical local models, or does the key-free lane need a special lightweight recipe so the first real run does not fail its own gates?
Does the cost-governance pillar interact with A8 — is 'first run free because it is local' a message the project wants to send?
